truth.description: Original procedural centerline network and opposite-flow tubes. Prescribed scatterer transport with deterministic outflow wrapping; no CFD, conservation-of-flow, anatomical or clinical claim. Tissue translates separately; vessel walls are not simulated.

metrics.label: Tissue rejection
metrics.scope: Same mixed-data projector applied to tissue-only oracle; energy over all pixels and times.

metrics.label: Blood retained
metrics.scope: Same mixed-data projector applied to blood-only oracle; energy, not vessel detection sensitivity.

metrics.label: Flow error
metrics.scope: MAE on valid pixels in guarded calibration-tube interiors.

metrics.label: Flow coverage
metrics.scope: Valid fraction of guarded tube-interior pixels.

metrics.label: Flow direction
metrics.scope: Among valid calibration-tube pixels; positive is toward probe.

metrics.label: Tissue shift
metrics.scope: Median valid tissue NCC estimate; known shift 0.43 mm.

metrics.label: Motion error
metrics.scope: Median absolute error on valid tissue-background windows.

metrics.label: Motion coverage
metrics.scope: Valid fraction of evaluation tissue windows.

metrics.label: Noise false detections
metrics.scope: Noise-only IQ, mixed-data projector and same absolute acceptance gates.

methods.title: Beamform once, reuse the delays
methods.formula: I(x,k) = (1/N) Σᵣ RFₐ(r, τ_TX(x) + τᵣ(x), k)
methods.variables: x: image position; k: frame index; r: receiver; τ: path length / sound speed; RFₐ: analytic RF; N=32. Gaussian carrier f₀=1 MHz, σ=0.7/f₀=0.7 µs; amplitude-spectrum FWHM ≈536 kHz.
methods.explanation: The same cached sample indices and interpolation fractions align the measured RF channels in every frame. Keep the complex result before envelope display.
methods.limitation: Homogeneous 1560 m/s, independent point scattering, one central divergent transmit. Attenuation and piston directivity use a center-frequency approximation despite the finite pulse bandwidth; not a plane-wave or full-wave solver.

methods.title: Separate dominant tissue motion
methods.formula: G = XᴴX; GV = V diag(σ²); Y = X(Id − V₂V₂ᴴ)
methods.variables: X: pixels × 32 complex frames; H: conjugate transpose; σ: singular values; V₂: first two temporal modes; Y: retained signal.
methods.explanation: A 32×32 Hermitian Gram decomposition supplies the same temporal subspace as SVD. Remove two modes, fixed before held-out tests; use no vessel mask.
methods.limitation: Tissue and blood can share temporal modes. Slow blood may be removed, and some tissue/noise remains. This is a fixed synthetic example, not adaptive clinical classification.

methods.title: Measure flow power and axial direction
methods.formula: P = meanₖ |Yₖ|²; R₁ = Σₖ Yₖ₊₁ conj(Yₖ); v_z = c arg(R₁)/(4πf₀Δt)
methods.variables: k: frame index; P: mean signal power; R₁: lag-one correlation; c=1560 m/s; f₀=1 MHz; Δt=2 ms between frames.
methods.explanation: Power reveals moving scatterers. Correlation phase estimates axial motion; accept pixels only above 3% of peak retained power and coherence 0.8.
methods.limitation: Near-axis approximation for this narrow aperture; angle bias, aliasing and decorrelation remain. Transverse velocity is not measured. Weak pixels are invalid, not stationary.

methods.title: Track tissue on the unfiltered branch
methods.variables: A: first-frame 9×5 envelope patch; B_d: shifted last-frame patch; bars: patch means; d: axial lag; physical shift = −d × pixel pitch.
methods.explanation: Search ±3 pixels in 0.1-pixel increments, then fit the local peak. Reject low-variance patches, boundary peaks, NCC below 0.8, or ambiguous peaks.
methods.limitation: Local rigid axial motion only; no strain, elasticity, out-of-plane displacement or clinical accuracy claim. This branch uses original IQ envelopes, never blood-filtered images.

compute.note: Measured offline Node stage times; operation counts are analytical travel-distance evaluations for direct versus cached geometry, not an observed speedup. Browser plays saved outputs.

assumptions: Original procedural phantom; prescribed trajectories, not anatomy or fluid dynamics. Network branches are independent scatterer streams with wrapping; no conservation or vessel-wall mechanics claim.
97-square image over 40 mm, 32 frames separated by 2 ms, 32 linear 0.6 mm-diameter pistons at 0.75 mm pitch, one central individual transmitter; no transmit compounding.

Homogeneous scalar straight paths at 1560 m/s. The Gaussian carrier has f₀=1 MHz and σ=0.7/f₀=0.7 µs, giving amplitude-spectrum FWHM ≈536 kHz. Piston directivity and brain-like attenuation use a center-frequency approximation. No refraction, multiple scattering or full-wave solver.
Scatterers are stationary during each echo acquisition. Tissue shifts by 0.43 mm over 62 ms; blood travels at prescribed centerline speeds, with ±40 mm/s in calibration tubes.

Tissue and blood amplitudes are seeded, blood amplitudes are one tenth as large. Gaussian receiver noise has independent per-frame seeds and fixed RMS 0.002 times the maximum noiseless channel amplitude across the ensemble.
Fast-time sampling is 8 MHz with a fixed origin and 1024 samples. Complex phase is preserved across frames; physical slow time differs from browser playback time.
Rank two was chosen in the disclosed earlier exploratory tube probe and frozen before the held-out seed/noise/translation cases saved in the validation report.
Tissue/blood oracle components and geometry masks are evaluation only; neither supplies the estimated image, SVD projector, velocity validity mask or motion validity mask.

Power comparisons share the unfiltered peak and -40 dB display floor; values below the floor are clipped only for display. B-mode cine uses one ensemble envelope peak and -55 dB floor. No per-frame normalization.
Positive axial velocity and displacement point toward the probe (+z). Phase velocity is a near-axis estimate, not full vector speed; invalid pixels are masked.
Source SHA-256 uses UTF-8 text with CRLF normalized to LF; binary hashes use raw bytes. Saved float32 references are compared with independent NumPy float64 calculations.
